label: Silica dust (concrete, stone, pool DE)
summary: Concrete, block, brick, mortar, tile, stone, sand and pool filter DE all contain crystalline silica. Cutting, grinding, drilling, crushing or tipping them dry makes fine dust that can hang in the air without a visible cloud and scars the lungs. Silicosis can't be reversed and can kill; it usually shows after years, but very heavy dust can bring it on within months, and silica also causes lung cancer, COPD and kidney disease.
signs: Cutting, grinding, drilling, chiselling or crushing concrete, block, brick, mortar, concrete or clay tile, or stone
Granite, quartz and engineered stone countertops: some engineered stone is up to 95% crystalline silica
Bagged concrete mix: one maker lists 60–100% quartz sand. Plain Portland cement holds little quartz, but the sand mixed with it does
Pool filter DE powder: one pool brand lists 35–50% cristobalite and another up to 70%; cristobalite is a form of crystalline silica, and one of them warns it may cause cancer if breathed in
Dried slurry and settled dust from earlier cutting, which puts silica back in the air when disturbed
Years after dusty work: shortness of breath, a lasting cough, weakness and weight loss
do: Cut and grind wet: a saw that feeds water onto the blade, or a steady spray where the tool hits, with enough water to keep visible dust down for the whole job
Work outdoors when you can. Wet cutting indoors may not keep the dust down, so add a fan that moves dusty air away from you
Choose lower-dust methods: a block splitter or hand tools instead of a saw, and as few cuts as possible
Clean up slurry before it dries, with a shovel or a wet vacuum with a HEPA filter. Wet dust down before sweeping, or use a HEPA vacuum
Where water meets electric tools, use a ground-fault (GFCI) outlet and sealed, watertight connections
Wash hands before breaks and before eating or drinking. Dust stays on clothing and can be breathed in again when clothes are put on or taken off
dont: Don't dry-sweep or blow dust off with compressed air
Don't trust water alone: it doesn't catch all the silica, so wear a respirator as well
Don't tip or mix pool DE or concrete mix in a closed room: do it outdoors or with good ventilation
Don't rely on a loose dust mask, or on any mask over a beard: a respirator only works sealed to a clean-shaven face
ppe: Sawing, even wet: HSE says an FFP3 mask or a half mask with P3 (P100) filters, protection factor 20. OSHA's floor for a wet saw indoors or over 4 hours a day is a filtering mask such as an N95, protection factor 10. Wear the better one you have, sealed to your face
A respirator only works sealed to a clean-shaven face
For tipping and mixing bagged concrete or pool DE: an N95 or better and tight-sealing goggles, as their makers advise when it's dusty
firstAid: You may feel nothing at the time; the harm comes from heavy or repeated dust. Get to fresh air, blow your nose to clear dust, and rinse dust out of the eyes with plenty of water, at least 15 minutes by one DE maker's sheet
Silicosis has no effective treatment, so keeping the dust out of your lungs is the only protection. A cough or breathlessness after dusty work means avoid dust from now on
Silicosis makes tuberculosis and other lung infections more likely; tell any doctor you ever see about past dust work
